subtitle: Lesson 12 · Complex Numbers & Complex Vector Spaces

steps.label: Plot a+bi as the point (a,b)
steps.sub: Horizontal axis is the real part, vertical is the imaginary part

steps.label: Modulus r: distance from the origin
Argument theta: angle from the positive real axis

caption: The same 3+4i from Lesson 11 — now described as 'how far, and in what direction' instead of 'how far right, how far up.'

code:
e^(i*theta) = cos(theta) + i*sin(theta)

polar to rectangular: r=2, theta=60 degrees
a = 2*cos(60) = 1
b = 2*sin(60) ~ 1.732
caption: e^(i theta) always lands on the unit circle — the standard shorthand for a modulus-1 complex number at angle theta.

steps.label: Each amplitude's argument is its phase
steps.sub: alpha|0> + beta|1> — alpha and beta each have their own theta

steps.label: Global phase (rotating both equally) is unobservable
steps.sub: Relative phase (the angle difference) is real and measurable
